statement.text:
A group is said to be X-critical if it does not belong to X but all its proper
subgroups belong to X. Let F be a soluble hereditary formation of finite groups for
which all F-critical groups are either groups of prime order or U-critical groups, where
U is the formation of all supersoluble finite groups. Must F be a saturated formation?
                                                                       S. F. Kamornikov
